customerJourneyStories.name: From loose tools to MijnVWE with Occasion Manager
customerJourneyStories.summary: A two-site dealer consolidates plate checks, RDW work and stock pricing on MijnVWE.

stages.narrative: A car bought at a trade-in turns out to have Belgian accident damage; the repair wipes out the margin and the owner realises his plate checks are incomplete.
Already uses VWE for RDW transactions (like many dealers since the 1980s); the account manager and a BOVAG-region peer mention Occasion Manager and damage history reports.
Compares Occasion Manager with Autotelex values and a free RDW open-data app; checks the €74.95 monthly price, the per-report fees and that it works on his phone at the lot.
Starts MijnVWE Welkom plus Occasion Manager for one month; runs damage history and appraisals on the next ten trade-ins in parallel with his old method.
Every purchase now starts with a plate scan in the PWA; the signal list drives Monday price changes and adverts flow to all portals from one entry.
Stays because the dossier, RDW actions and adverts are in one place and stand-time fell; adds the dealer website and recommends VWE in the regional dealer group chat.

stages.narrative: Leads arrive in three mailboxes and buyers who need a loan leave to arrange it at their bank; the owner notices fewer closed deals.
Sees the "Website autobedrijf" and "Auto's financieren" modules inside MijnVWE and hears from VWE in October 2025 that Financial Lease Partner is the new financing partner.
Compares the VWE website with a local web agency and a portal's dealer site on price, live stock, lead routing and whether financing quotes can be shown per car.
Launches the website and the finance widget for one month and tracks leads and finance applications alongside the old site.
All enquiries land in one lead inbox; every quote shows a monthly payment and applications go straight to the lender.
Keeps both modules because conversion improved and commission covers the subscription; asks for SMS follow-ups.

customerJourneyStories.name: Group rollout of Occasion Manager and market insight
customerJourneyStories.summary: A 14-branch holding standardises used-car pricing on VWE.

stages.narrative: Year-end shows 30% of group stock older than 90 days and three branches undercutting each other on identical models.
The formula's purchasing director hears VWE present the Nationaal Occasion Onderzoek at an industry event; the VWE account manager follows up with a Market Performance Manager demo.
Compares VWE with INDICATA and Autotelex on data coverage, branch pricing model (€250 setup, per-branch fee), DMS integration and the neutrality of RDW-based share data; IT checks SSO and data terms.
Pilots Occasion Manager and the occasion performance meter in three branches for a quarter, comparing stand-time with three control branches.
Monday group meetings run on the stock and signal list; branch managers get monthly market-share reports.
Renews the group contract and extends to all branches because stand-time fell in pilot branches; adds change-of-ownership lead lists for the brand dealerships.

customerJourneyStories.name: Moving BPM and export work to VWE after the XRAY acquisition
customerJourneyStories.summary: An importer of German premium cars consolidates BPM, taxation and export documents.

stages.narrative: A Belastingdienst correction on three imports costs more than the profit on those cars; the trader wants defensible taxation reports.
Already used XRAY for taxations; the April 2026 announcement that VWE acquired XRAY and the VWE account manager point to combined BPM, valuation and export services.
Compares XRAY/VWE with Autotelex BPM tools and his independent appraiser on report acceptance, price per taxation, turnaround and whether history checks are included.
Runs the next five imports through XRAY taxation and VWE export documents, comparing assessed BPM and lead time.
Every import starts with history and a BPM calculation; export documents are ordered online instead of at the counter.
Stays because one account covers BPM, documents and RDW transactions; starts listing slow movers on the trade platform.

customerJourneyStories.name: From web forms to API-driven fleet administration
customerJourneyStories.summary: A mid-sized lessor automates RDW actions and remarketing with VWE.

stages.narrative: Fleet growth means 600 RDW actions a month done by hand in web forms; two fines for late indemnification reach the board.
The fleet software vendor mentions VWE APIs; the lease company also sees VWE listed as the largest recognised RDW provider.
Compares VWE with its current provider and RDW open data on API coverage, authorisation model, SLA, security review and price per transaction; legal checks data licence terms.
Runs a three-month pilot: transfers and enrichment via API for one fleet segment and damage calculation on returns.
RDW transactions run from the fleet system; monthly enrichment keeps master data aligned; returns get a damage estimate and valuation automatically.
